exercise.name: Chest-Supported Reverse Fly
library_steps: Lie face down on a flat or low incline bench, dumbbells hanging down.
Raise your arms out to the sides, elbows slightly bent.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top, then lower slowly.
exercise.one_line_summary: Chest down on a 30 deg incline bench, feet on the floor: dumbbells hang straight down (start), then arms rise out to the sides to about shoulder level, elbows softly bent, shoulder blades squeezed (end).

setup.target: Low incline, chest on the pad, chin just past the top, feet on the floor.
setup.tolerance: pad 0-45 deg (library flat/low; ACE seated version 45-60)

setup.target: Palms facing each other at the bottom; thumbs toward the head.

movement.measure: arm angle from hanging straight down (world) to level
movement.end: about 90 deg (arms level, out to the sides, in line with the ears or a little in front)

movement.measure: still: feet on the floor either side of the seat

muscles.role: Main mover of horizontal abduction; prone horizontal abduction ~42% MVIC (S2).
Squeeze the shoulder blades together; middle trap ~51% MVIC in prone horizontal abduction (S2); top MT exercise in S3.
Rotator cuff steadies the humeral head.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Back arches and the torso comes up as the arms rise.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Momentum and the lower back do the work.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbows bend a lot and pull back.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Lats and biceps take over from the rear delts.

sources.citation: American Council on Exercise. Incline Reverse Fly (exercise library).
sources.what_it_gave: Torso on the pad (45-60 deg), arms hang, palms facing, elbows slightly bent, raise to near shoulder level in line with or slightly in front of the ears, squeeze the shoulder blades, keep torso on pad.

sources.citation: Kim S, Kang M. 2020. Influence of pre-emptive scapular posterior tilt on scapular muscle activation and scapulohumeral movements during shoulder horizontal abduction in the prone position. J Int Acad Phys Ther Res 11(4):2173-2177.
sources.what_it_gave: General prone horizontal abduction (n=15): middle trap 50.6, lower trap 58.2, posterior deltoid 41.9 % MVIC.

sources.citation: Ekstrom RA, Donatelli RA, Soderberg GL. 2003. Surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258.
sources.what_it_gave: Middle trapezius highest in prone shoulder horizontal extension with external rotation (and prone overhead raise).

clip_check.check: Start: arms hang vertically under the shoulders
End: arms level, out to the sides
clip_check.target: 80-95 deg from hanging; hands not above shoulder height

clip_check.check: Chest on the pad in both pictures
Thighs clear of pad and seat; feet flat on floor
Hands on the handles; dumbbells clear of bench and floor
Rear delts the strongest red in both pictures
